text: Daniel "saw a dream and visions of his head while on his bed. Then he wrote down the dream."
explanation:
We imagine visions must be spectacular: an angel appearing, the room glowing, everyone present seeing it too. But Daniel, to whom God gave "understanding in all visions and dreams," received many of his while lying in bed, as thoughts came to his mind. Even Paul's companions on the Damascus road didn't see what he saw.

God said, "If there is a prophet among you, I, the Lord, make Myself known to him in a vision; I speak to him in a dream." What was once reserved for prophets is now the inheritance of every believer. When you pray, expect gentle pictures to rise from within. Don't dismiss them. Write them down, and test them against the Word later.

text: God never makes your mind passive and takes you over. He works with your will, never around it.
explanation:
The occult has "automatic writing": blank the mind, surrender the will, and let a spirit move the pen. The devil always copies God's ways, with one difference: God never overrides your choice. Even tongues require you to speak. You stay fully yourself, in your right mind, a co-worker with God.

So ask Him in faith: "How do You see my marriage? My work? Me?" Pray in the Spirit, then watch and listen, and write down what comes. A new covenant word will always lead to "edification and exhortation and comfort." Even a warning from God comes with His peace and a way forward. Fearful pictures that leave you crushed aren't from Him; bind them in Jesus' name.

text: The blessed man "will not see when heat comes." The cursed man "shall not see when good comes."
explanation:
Jeremiah paints two pictures. The one who trusts in the Lord "shall be like a tree planted by the waters… and will not fear when heat comes; but her leaf will be green, and will not be anxious in the year of drought." The heat still comes, but he isn't fixed on it. The man who trusts in man "shall be like a shrub in the desert, and shall not see when good comes." Good comes, but he can't see it.

Some people can find a problem in every solution, a hidden motive behind every kindness, a fault in every spouse. Choose to look for the good: in your family, your colleagues, even this season. That isn't denying reality; it's seeing the reality the cursed man misses.

text: "The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree, grow like a cedar… they shall still bear fruit in old age; they shall be fresh."
explanation:
God speaks in pictures so they can fill your heart. The date palm stands tall and keeps producing fruit well into its old age. Some cedars are over a thousand years old, still strong, still fragrant. "Those who are planted in the house of the Lord… shall still bear fruit in old age; they shall be fresh and flourishing": the word means luxuriantly green.

And Isaiah adds, "As the days of a tree, so shall be the days of My people." Some olive trees live for two thousand years. Let these be the images you carry of your future: not frailty and decline, but fruitfulness, freshness and strength.

text: "Your children like olive plants around your table." Olive growers renew an old tree with young shoots.
explanation:
God could simply have said, "Your children will be a blessing." Instead He gives a picture to study. An olive tree is useful in every part (fruit, oil, wood, leaves), and it's famous for living very long. When an olive tree grows old, young shoots growing from its base take over and the tree carries on for centuries; some in the Garden of Gethsemane are extremely old.

Children renew our youth. And "your wife shall be like a fruitful vine": the vine gives grapes, and grapes give wine, so she will delight and intoxicate you. If that isn't how things look right now, don't describe your family as they appear. Describe them as God sees them.

text: In Eden, eyes opened by the wrong tree saw nakedness. At Emmaus, eyes opened at the breaking of bread saw Him.
explanation:
God crowned man "with glory and honour," and Adam and Eve lived wrapped in that glory. But they ate from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, "the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked": they saw their lack and their shame. God had wanted their eyes opened through the tree of life.

On resurrection day, Jesus walked with two disciples, a husband and wife perhaps, just as God once walked with the first couple. At their table "He took bread, blessed and broke it… Then their eyes were opened and they knew Him." The Lord's Supper is your tree of life. Each time you partake, don't see your lack. See Him, and all His supply.

text: Fill your heart with God's pictures, or something else will fill it for you.
explanation:
You were designed to be shaped by pictures. If your heart isn't filled with the images God gives in His Word, a vine, a palm tree, a shield, a table prepared, it won't stay empty. Hours of violence, betrayal and bad news will supply the pictures instead, and then you lie down at night with dread, suspicion and a gloomy view of the future.

Relax with your family and enjoy good things, but guard what you feed your imagination. Spend time in the Word and listening to it. One word from God can change your life, and one picture from Him can replace years of fear.
